uninstall.title: Uninstall Memlore
uninstall.hint: Permanently erase every journal, entry, photo and setting stored on this computer.
uninstall.modal_body: This deletes your encrypted vault and everything in it. There is no undo, and no copy is kept anywhere on this computer.
uninstall.app_not_removable_macos: The application cannot delete itself from this location. Move Memlore to the Trash manually after it quits.
uninstall.app_not_removable_windows: Your data will be erased. Remove the application itself from Settings → Apps → Installed apps.
uninstall.app_not_removable_linux: Your data will be erased. Remove the application itself with your package manager.
uninstall.app_not_removable_other: Your data will be erased. Removing the application itself is not supported on this platform.
uninstall.cloud_note: Data synced to Google Drive or iCloud is left untouched — other devices keep working. Disconnect sync first if you want it gone too.
uninstall.skipped_label: Will NOT be deleted — outside the area Memlore is allowed to erase
uninstall.stalled: Memlore could not quit on its own. Your data is being erased in the background — please quit the app manually.
uninstall.loading: Checking what is stored on this computer…

about_section.heading_description: A little life. A lasting story.
about_section.description: A cross-platform, privacy-first, local-first journal — with rich, optional AI.

principles.local_first: Local-first — works fully offline. Your entries stay on your device.
principles.private: Private — encrypted at rest. No Memlore server, no account, no telemetry.
principles.ai_optional: Optional AI — off until you opt in. Your provider, including on-device.
principles.yours: Yours — sync through your own Drive if you want. Export anytime.

about_section.license: Free & open source under AGPL-3.0-or-later — see LICENSE in the repository.

media_view.title: Gallery layout
media_view.description: How the Media view opens. Full page shows a wide grid; Two panel keeps the entry editor beside the grid.

media_cache.limit_hint: Max size for cached media; oldest files are evicted first.
media_cache.clear_hint: Remove all cached media files. Cloud-backed images will be re-downloaded on next view.
media_cache.clear_confirm: Clear the cache of full-size images? Cloud-backed images will be re-downloaded on next view. Small thumbnails are kept for fast browsing, and images waiting to be uploaded are never affected.

media_upload_limits.title: Per-file upload size limits
media_upload_limits.hint: Maximum size for each individual photo or video before it enters your journal — not a total across media.
media_upload_limits.help: Each file is checked when you insert media. The backend stores limits in bytes; the smallest allowed value is 1 MB. Use Unlimited to disable a per-file limit.
media_upload_limits.photo_hint: Photos over the limit are recompressed automatically and only blocked if they still don't fit.
media_upload_limits.video_hint: Videos over the limit are blocked — Memlore does not transcode video.
media_upload_limits.warning: Large media consumes your cloud storage quota fast. Consider a smaller limit.

cloud.hint: Sync entries through a cloud service you control. Your data is end-to-end encrypted before leaving your device.

gdrive.name: Google Drive
gdrive.description: Sync through a private folder on your Google account.

icloud.name: iCloud Drive
icloud.description: Sync through iCloud Drive on this Mac.

local.name: Local folder
local.description: Sync through a folder you choose — a drive, NAS, or shared directory.

cloud.icloud_unavailable_hint: Sign in to iCloud Drive in System Settings to use this option

errors.already_connected: Disconnect the current cloud service before connecting another.
errors.permission_denied: Grant Memlore access to iCloud Drive in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Files and Folders, then retry.

gdrive.storage_app_usage_tooltip: Space used by Memlore on Google Drive
gdrive.storage_drive_free_tooltip: {{free}} free of {{total}} on your Google account

storage_quota_notice.title: Google Drive storage is almost full
storage_quota_notice.body: New media uploads may fail. Review your media cache settings and upload size limits.

disconnect_modal.title: Disconnect {{provider}}?
disconnect_modal.body: Stop syncing this device. Your local journal entries, photos, and notes stay intact. Files already on the cloud copy are not deleted.
disconnect_modal.body_gdrive_note: To reconnect, you will need to sign in to Google again.

errors.password_required: Enter your journal password to connect {{provider}}.
errors.timed_out: Authorization timed out. Please try again and complete sign-in within 5 minutes.
errors.keyring_mismatch: The encryption key on {{provider}} was created with a different password. Enter the password you used when you first set up Memlore on your other device.
errors.keyring_corrupted: The encryption key file on {{provider}} is corrupted. Disconnect, manually delete .meta/keyring.json from the Memlore folder, then reconnect.
errors.v1_wiped_reconnect: An older keyring format was found and removed. Please reconnect Google Drive to complete the upgrade.

reset.modal_body: Marks entries, journals, and media this device owns for re-upload on the next sync. Nothing is deleted on this device or the cloud copy. This only resets sync tracking — it does not replace the full copy on either side.
reset.success: Reset complete. {{entries}} entries, {{media}} media items, and {{journals}} journals will re-upload on the next sync.
reset.queued: Reset queued. It will run when the current sync finishes.

cloud_to_local.modal_body: Memlore will download and verify the complete cloud copy, create a local recovery backup, then replace synced data on this device. If download or verification fails, your current local data stays unchanged. Settings and secrets that only belong to this device are preserved. After success, normal sync continues from the restored copy. Close Memlore on other devices first so they do not push stale data.
cloud_to_local.checking: Checking readiness and preparing a local backup…
cloud_to_local.ready: Ready. A local recovery backup has been prepared. Confirm to download, verify, and replace synced data on this device.
cloud_to_local.success: This device was replaced from {{provider}}. Normal sync can continue.

local_to_cloud.modal_body: Memlore will create a local recovery backup, check that every item on this device is complete, then permanently delete Memlore data on {{provider}} and rebuild it from this device. Your local data on this device is preserved. If a check fails before deletion, {{provider}} is left unchanged. Other devices must reconnect before they can sync again. Close Memlore on other devices first.
local_to_cloud.checking: Checking readiness and creating a local recovery backup…
local_to_cloud.ready: Ready. A local recovery backup was created. Confirm to delete {{provider}} data and rebuild it from this device.
local_to_cloud.success: {{provider}} was rebuilt from this device. Other devices must reconnect before they can sync again.

delete_and_disconnect.modal_body: Permanently deletes Memlore data from {{provider}} and disconnects this device. Local data on this device stays and will not upload again until you reconnect. Other devices that remain connected may re-upload on their next sync — disconnect them too if you want a fully empty cloud.
delete_and_disconnect.backup_warning: This permanently deletes the cloud copy. After deletion, the copy on this device is your only copy — export a backup first (Settings → Data → Export) if you need one.
delete_and_disconnect.success: {{provider}} data deleted. You are now disconnected.
delete_and_disconnect.error_sync_in_progress: A sync is currently running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.

recovery.title: Recovery in progress
recovery.busy: Another recovery action is already in progress.
recovery.blocked_sync_in_progress: A sync is running right now. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
recovery.blocked_not_connected: {{provider}} is not connected on this device. Connect it, then try again.
recovery.blocked_force_re_pair: This device has to reconnect to {{provider}} first. Finish reconnecting, then try again.
recovery.blocked_rotation_active: A security key change is still running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
recovery.blocked_competing_recovery: A recovery is already in progress on {{provider}}. Wait for it to finish before continuing.
recovery.blocked_cloud_outdated: The cloud copy is older than what this device expects, so restoring from it would lose data.
recovery.blocked_cloud_outdated_use_local: The cloud copy is older than what this device expects, so restoring from it would lose data. Use “Replace {{provider}} with this device” instead.
recovery.blocked_cloud_inconsistent: The cloud copy is in an inconsistent state. Let your devices finish syncing, then try again.
recovery.blocked_other_job_active: Another recovery is already in progress on this device. Finish or cancel it, then try again.
recovery.blocked_insufficient_disk: Not enough free disk space — about {{needed}} is needed but only {{available}} is free. Free up some space, then try again.
recovery.blocked_media_incomplete: Some media files on this device are missing or damaged ({{missing}} missing, {{corrupt}} damaged). Restore or remove them, then try again.
recovery.blocked_cloud_unreadable: Memlore could not read the cloud copy. Check your internet connection, then try again.
recovery.blocked_backup_failed: Memlore could not create the local recovery backup, so it stopped before changing anything.
recovery.failed_lease_lost: This device lost its claim on the recovery — another device may have taken over on {{provider}}. Close Memlore on your other devices before continuing.
recovery.failed_local_media_unreadable: Some media files on this device could not be read from disk. Restore or remove them before continuing.
recovery.failed_key_unavailable: Memlore could not access this device's encryption key. Make sure the app is unlocked, then continue.
recovery.failed_cloud_media_incomplete: Some media files could not be downloaded from {{provider}} ({{missing}} missing, {{corrupt}} damaged). Nothing on this device was replaced.
recovery.failed_upload_incomplete: Some items could not be uploaded to {{provider}}. Check your internet connection, then continue the recovery.
recovery.failed_fence_release: The transfer finished, but Memlore could not release the recovery lock on {{provider}}. Close Memlore on your other devices, then continue.
recovery.failed_lease_unconfirmed: Memlore could not confirm the state of the recovery lock on {{provider}}. Try continuing again.
recovery.failed_recovery_superseded: This recovery was ended — another recovery took over the cloud copy while this one was finishing. You can start again if you still need to.

errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

triage.question: What is going wrong?
triage.stuck_title: Sync seems stuck or some items never upload
triage.stuck_hint: Re-upload what this device owns on the next sync. Nothing is deleted anywhere.
triage.device_wrong_title: This device is wrong — {{provider}} has the copy I trust
triage.device_wrong_hint: Download and verify the cloud copy, then replace synced data on this device.
triage.cloud_wrong_title: {{provider}} is wrong — this device has the copy I trust
triage.cloud_wrong_hint: Delete Memlore data on {{provider}} and rebuild it from this device.
triage.stop_title: I want to stop syncing on this device
triage.stop_hint: Disconnect {{provider}}, and choose whether the cloud copy stays.

stop.question: What should happen to the copy on {{provider}}?
stop.keep_title: Keep it — just disconnect this device
stop.keep_hint: Stop syncing this device. Data on this device and data already on {{provider}} are both kept.
stop.delete_hint: Permanently delete Memlore data from {{provider}} and disconnect this device. Local data stays on this device and will not upload again until you reconnect.

disconnect.done: This device is disconnected from {{provider}}. Your local journal stays intact; files already on {{provider}} were kept.

scope_upgrade.title: Google Drive sync upgraded
scope_upgrade.body: We moved your synced data into a private folder Google manages just for Memlore — it is no longer visible in your My Drive. Click Connect to re-upload your journal entries. Your local data is safe.
scope_upgrade.note: Your previous Memlore folder inside My Drive is no longer used. You can delete it manually if you want.

token_revoked.title: Google Drive access expired
token_revoked.body: Your Google Drive sign-in is no longer valid — it was revoked from your Google account, or it expired after a long period without syncing. Reconnect to continue syncing.

cross_mode.needs_password_title: Sync folder is encrypted with a password
cross_mode.needs_password_body: This device is in no-password mode, but the cloud folder was set up by a password-protected device. Set a password in Security to unlock the synced entries — or disconnect from this cloud folder.
cross_mode.needs_password_note: Want the cloud folder to be unencrypted too? Open the device that set up the cloud folder, remove its password in Settings → Security, then sync once. After that, this device can disconnect, wipe the cloud folder manually from drive.google.com, and reconnect.
cross_mode.needs_no_password_body: This device is in password mode, but the cloud folder was set up by a no-password device. Remove the password in Security to read these entries — or disconnect from this cloud folder.
cross_mode.needs_no_password_note: Want the cloud folder to be password-protected too? Open the device that set up the cloud folder, set a password in Settings → Security, then sync once. After that, this device can disconnect, wipe the cloud folder manually from drive.google.com, and reconnect.

security.encryption_callout: Your journal is end-to-end encrypted with AES-256-GCM. A password is required and cannot be disabled — we have no way to recover your data if you lose it.

secure_wizard.card_caption: Tell Memlore what happened and get the right steps to secure your journal.

errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.sync_in_progress: A sync is currently running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.

diagrams.two_devices: Two devices connected to the same encrypted journal through the cloud
diagrams.key_rotated: An old encryption key replaced by a new encryption key
diagrams.cloud_cut: The other device disconnected from the cloud
diagrams.phrase_new: A new 24-word recovery phrase replacing the old phrase

triage.question: What happened?
triage.words_title: I think my 24 recovery words leaked
triage.words_hint: Someone may have seen or copied the words that unlock your whole journal.
triage.password_title: I think my device password leaked
triage.password_hint: Someone may know the password that unlocks Memlore on this device.
triage.device_title: A device is lost, stolen, or compromised
triage.device_hint: Stop another device from reading new entries or reaching your cloud files.
triage.routine_hint: Create a fresh master key for future entries as a precaution, without changing your recovery words.

words.body: The 24 words are a second key to your whole journal. Resetting them creates a new master key and 24 new words for future entries.
words.reset_body: Enter your current device password. Memlore will show the new words once, so be ready to save them safely.
words.running: Creating a new master key and recovery phrase…
words.done_body: New entries now use the new master key. Keep the new 24 words safe and re-pair your other devices.

password.body: This password unlocks the journal stored on this device. It does not travel to other devices and, by itself, does not expose your synced data.
password.device_question: Do you think someone may have reached a device?
password.change_body: Choose a new password for this device. Other devices keep their own passwords.
password.change_success_body: This device now unlocks with your new password.

device.picker_empty: No other devices are paired with this journal.
device.words_question: Were the 24 recovery words stored on or kept with this device?
device.words_yes: Yes, the words may have leaked too
device.words_no: No, the recovery words are safe
device.scope_title: How completely do you need to cut off this device?
device.scope_revoke_hint: Rotate the master key. The device keeps old local data and its Google access.
device.scope_cutoff_title: Cut it off from Google completely
device.scope_cutoff_hint: Revoke it, disconnect Memlore, remove Google access, then reconnect this device.
device.words_remove_title: Nothing happened — just remove it from the list
device.words_remove_hint: No keys change and no credentials are needed. Use this when the device is retired or wiped and still in your hands.

remove.confirm_body: This only removes the device from the list. No keys change, and you won't be asked for a password. The device keeps its data and access.
remove.confirm_reappear: If it syncs again, it will reappear. Go back and pick a security option if you need to cut it off.
remove.busy_other: Another device removal is still in progress — wait for it to finish first.
remove.queued_sync: Sync is running — the removal has been queued and will run as soon as sync finishes.
remove.running: Removing the device from the list…
remove.done_fact_list: The device no longer appears in your device list.
remove.done_fact_unchanged: Nothing else changed — it keeps its local data, its keys, and its cloud access.
remove.done_fact_reappear: If it syncs with this journal again, it will show up in the list again.

revoke.confirm_body: Confirm with your current recovery phrase and device password to revoke {{device}}. This rotates the master key for new entries.
revoke.running: Revoking the device and rotating the master key…
revoke.done_fact_new_entries: That device can no longer read new entries.
revoke.done_fact_old_data: It can still read every entry written before now — both what is stored on it and anything it downloads from the cloud, because that data keeps its old key.
revoke.done_fact_cloud_access: Its Google access is still live, so it can delete or overwrite cloud files through Google Drive.
revoke.cutoff_google: Cut it off from Google too

cutoff.step1_body: First, rotate the master key so the affected device cannot read new entries.
cutoff.step2_body: Disconnect Google Drive inside Memlore, then remove Memlore's access from your Google Account.
cutoff.step2_not_sufficient: Disconnecting inside Memlore may not cancel the login token stored on the other device. Both the in-app disconnect and removing access at Google are required.
cutoff.step2_no_delete_reassurance: Nothing is deleted from this device or Google Drive. Step 3 reconnects this device and will not ask for your 24 recovery words.
cutoff.step3_body: Reconnect this device with its current password. Your journal data stays in Google Drive, so no full re-upload or recovery phrase is expected.
cutoff.done_body: It cannot read new entries and its saved Google access has been removed. Data already stored locally on that device may still be readable.

routine.intro_body: Nothing is wrong. This creates a fresh master key that encrypts only the entries you write from now on — entries you already have keep the old key and are not re-encrypted. Your 24 recovery words do not change, and other devices must re-pair with them.
routine.confirm_body: Enter your current recovery phrase and device password to continue.

security.status_password_on_desc: Entries are encrypted with your password.

invisible_lock.title: Invisible lock
invisible_lock.description: Hide selected entries and journals in separate password-protected vaults. Only one vault is open at a time; while locked, the app behaves as if that content does not exist.
invisible_lock.open_description: Enter a password to open a matching vault, or create a new empty one if none matches. The app never tells you which happened.
invisible_lock.no_recovery_warning: Remember each vault password — they cannot be recovered or reset. If you forget a password, you permanently lose access to that vault's content. Invisible lock is not extra encryption.
invisible_lock.change_description: Re-key the open vault. If the new password already opens another vault, this vault's items merge into that one.
invisible_lock.change_modal_description: Enter the current password for the open vault, then choose a new one.
invisible_lock.remove_empty_description: Delete vaults that have no entries and no journals. Always available; no counts are shown.
invisible_lock.remove_empty_confirm_body: Vaults with no entries and no journals will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
invisible_lock.auto_lock_description: Close the open vault after this much inactivity.

your_password.title: What does my device password do?
your_password.body: It unlocks Memlore on this device. Each phone or computer can have its own password — you never share it. Changing your password here only updates the lock on this device. Your entries stay as they are.

recovery_phrase.title: What is the 24-word recovery phrase?
recovery_phrase.body: During setup we show you 24 words once. Save them somewhere safe — they link all your devices to the same journal. You need this phrase to add a new device or to reconnect after a security change. Memlore never stores it; only you have it.

on_device_and_cloud.title: How is my journal protected on this device and in the cloud?
on_device_and_cloud.body: On this device, your journal is encrypted before it is saved to disk. When you turn on sync, each entry is encrypted again before it leaves your device. Google Drive or iCloud only receives scrambled copies — they cannot read your journal.

adding_device.title: How do I add another device?
adding_device.body: Install Memlore on the new device and sign in to the same cloud account. Enter your 24-word recovery phrase and choose a password for that device. Your password on your other device stays private — you never need to share it.

changing_password.title: What happens when I change my password?
changing_password.body: Only the lock on this device changes. Your entries stay encrypted as they are, and other devices keep their own passwords. This does not cut off other devices and does not rotate encryption keys.

second_lock.title: How does second lock work?
second_lock.body: Second lock is an extra password inside the app, behind your device password. Mark entries or whole journals as second-locked and they stay hidden from the sidebar, calendar, search, and media gallery until you enter the second-lock password for this session. It hides content from view — it does not add separate encryption. You can show covered placeholders so you know something is locked, or hide locked items completely. Auto-lock hides them again after idle time. There is no recovery if you forget this password.

invisible_lock.title: How does invisible lock work?
invisible_lock.body: Invisible lock uses separate password-protected vaults. Each password opens (or creates) its own vault; only one vault can be open at a time. While a vault is closed, its entries and journals do not appear anywhere — lists, search, calendar, tags, footer eye — the app behaves as if they do not exist. Opening a vault uses open-or-create: a matching password opens that vault; a new password creates an empty vault. The footer eye appears only while a vault is unlocked and only locks it. You can mark an entry invisible while locked (password + confirm) without revealing the rest of that vault. Changing a password to one that already opens another vault merges items into that vault. Invisible lock is not encryption and has no recovery. Use a different password from second lock.

second_vs_invisible.title: Second lock or invisible lock — which should I use?
second_vs_invisible.body: Use second lock when you want to hide specific content but may still want a hint that something is there (covered placeholders). Use invisible lock when you need maximum discretion — separate vaults that leave no trace until the right password is entered. You can use both on different items. Both require a device password first.

scenario_shared_device.title: Someone else sometimes uses my computer
scenario_shared_device.body: Set a device password so the app locks when closed. Second-lock entries or journals you do not want visible while the app is open. Turn on auto-lock so second-locked content hides again when you step away.

scenario_private_entries.title: I want some entries hidden but others easy to find
scenario_private_entries.body: Leave everyday entries unlocked. Second-lock the sensitive ones. Optionally turn on "Show existence of locked entries" to see covered placeholders in the calendar and lists as a reminder.

scenario_hidden_journal.title: I want a whole journal that nobody should know exists
scenario_hidden_journal.body: Open or create an invisible vault with a password, then mark the journal invisible while that vault is open. Until you open that vault again, the journal and its entries vanish from every view — including the footer, which shows the eye only while unlocked.

removing_device.title: What happens when I revoke a lost device?
removing_device.body: Open Secure my journal and pick “A device is lost, stolen, or compromised”. Revoking a device rotates the master key so it cannot read new entries. It can still read journal data already stored on it, and it may still reach the cloud copy — through Google Drive, iCloud, or a synced folder — until you also cut off that session. The wizard walks you through the right cutoff for the cloud service you use: disconnect inside Memlore, then revoke Google access or sign the lost device out of iCloud (or change the Apple ID password). Your other devices must re-pair with your recovery phrase. If a device is simply retired and still in your hands, none of this is needed — pick “Nothing happened — just remove it from the list” in the same wizard to tidy the device list without touching your keys.

rotating_master_key.title: What happens when I rotate the master key?
rotating_master_key.body: Open Secure my journal and pick “Nothing happened — routine key rotation”. Memlore creates fresh keys for new entries. Your 24-word recovery phrase stays the same. Older entries are not re-uploaded or re-encrypted. Your other devices must enter the recovery phrase to reconnect before they can read new entries.

secure_my_journal.title: How does Secure my journal help?
secure_my_journal.body: Use Secure my journal in Security actions for any incident. It asks what happened — your 24 recovery words leaked, your device password leaked, a device is lost or compromised, or you just want a routine key rotation — then guides you to the right steps, including what each step cannot undo.

if_you_lose.title: What if I forget my password and lose my recovery phrase?
if_you_lose.body: Your journal cannot be recovered. There is no backdoor and no support reset. Save your recovery phrase somewhere safe — a password manager or paper in a drawer.

scenario_lost_extra_lock.title: What if I forget my second-lock or invisible-lock password?
scenario_lost_extra_lock.body: Those passwords cannot be reset or recovered. If you forget a second-lock password or any invisible-vault password, access to that locked content is permanently lost. The rest of your journal remains available through your device password and recovery phrase.

revoke.cloud_guidance_icloud_step1: On the lost device, go to Settings → [your name] → Sign Out. Or change your Apple ID password at appleid.apple.com to invalidate all sessions.
revoke.cloud_guidance_icloud_step2: iCloud Drive access is tied to the Apple ID session — signing out or revoking the session removes all iCloud access.
revoke.cloud_guidance_generic: Sign out the lost device from the cloud provider it uses, or change the account credentials to invalidate its session.

reset.forward_only: This is forward-only: it protects everything written after the reset and nothing written before it. Older entries stay readable with the phrase they were saved under.

reset.new_phrase_body: Your recovery phrase has been reset. These are your NEW 24 words — your old phrase no longer works. This is the only time they are shown, so save them now. Every other device will need these new words once to keep reading new entries.

rotate.warning: Rotating the master key generates a new encryption key for new entries. Your current 24-word recovery phrase is unchanged. Every other synced device will need to re-pair before it can read new entries.

rotate.i_saved_checkbox: I have written down and safely stored my recovery phrase.

second_lock.intro_body: Second lock hides selected entries and journals from every view and from search until you enter a second password. It sits behind the master password; it is not separate encryption.

warmup.title: Warming up your local model
warmup.explainer: Your local model is warming up. This takes a few seconds and only happens on first use of the session or after about 10 minutes of inactivity — subsequent replies are instant.
warmup.privacy_note: Runs fully on-device — nothing leaves your machine.

media_compression.photo_hint: Shrink inserted photos to save disk and sync space.
media_compression.photo_help: EXIF date and GPS are preserved so the metadata suggestion flows keep working. HEIC and SVG pass through untouched.

photo_desc.off: Store every photo at its original size and quality. Best when you have plenty of disk space and want to keep pixel-perfect originals.
photo_desc.standard: Resize to 2400 px (longer edge) and re-encode at JPEG quality 85. Typical iPhone photos drop ~6× in size with negligible visible loss.
photo_desc.aggressive: Resize to 1600 px and re-encode at JPEG quality 75. Smaller files, slightly more visible compression — good for sync-bandwidth-constrained setups.
photo_desc.custom: Set your own maximum edge length and JPEG quality below.

media_compression.custom_photo_hint: Lower max edge and quality give smaller files but more visible loss.
media_compression.max_edge_hint: Photos with the longer side bigger than this are scaled down.
media_compression.quality_hint: 40 = small + noticeably soft. 100 = near-lossless, files barely shrink.
media_compression.video_hint: Shrink inserted videos to save disk and sync space.
media_compression.video_help: Transcodes to H.264 .mp4 using the OS video engine. macOS only — on other platforms videos are stored unchanged. A clip that would not get smaller keeps its original file.

video_desc.off: Store every video at its original size and quality. Best when you have plenty of disk space.
video_desc.standard: Downscale to 960 × 540 and re-encode as H.264 .mp4. Big savings for phone clips with little visible loss. macOS only.
video_desc.aggressive: Downscale to 640 × 480 H.264 .mp4. Smallest files, more visible compression — good for sync-bandwidth-constrained setups. macOS only.
video_desc.custom: Set your own maximum edge below; it maps to the nearest H.264 preset. macOS only.

media_compression.custom_video_hint: Lower max edge gives smaller files but lower resolution.
media_compression.video_max_edge_hint: Mapped to the nearest H.264 preset (480p, 540p, 720p, 1080p).
